newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia to start national airline by end of 1997.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia to start national airline by end of 1997.

text.p: The Slovak government has approved the creation of a national airline, which should begin operating by the end of this year, the Ministry of Transport said on Wednesday.
"The airline, Slovenske Aerolinie a.s. (SA), has been created as a joint-stock company, in which the state will hold a controlling stake," Ministry Spokesman Emil Picha told Reuters.

Devin Group s.r.o., a subsidiary of Devin Banka -- which is responsible for managing repayment of Russian debt to Slovakia -- holds 33.5 percent of the airline's 1.3 million crown basic capital, he added.
Wili a.s., a tourist agency focusing mainly on Russia, owns 28.9 percent in the airline, while Russian aircraft constructor OKB Yakovlev holds 3.2 percent.
The state will control the remaining 34.4 percent, either directly or through state-controlled domestic companies, Picha said.

The state will provide the carrier with an unspecified number of Russian-built aircraft as a part of the repayment of extensive Russian debts to Slovakia, mostly inherited from the communist period of the former Council for Mutual Economic Assistance (COMECON).

Slovakia has been trying to set up a national carrier since the split of the Czechoslovakia in 1993, when the Czech Republic retained control over the former Czechoslovak Airlines (CSA), now known as Ceska Aerolinie a.s..

SA hopes to transport some 85,000 passengers this year, rising to an estimated 200,000 by the year 2000, Picha said. He added the company will also provide cargo transport, but declined to elaborate on estimated volumes.
The overall number of passengers in several small domestic carriers totalled 110,000 in 1995, while an estimated 180,000 Slovaks flew with foreign airlines from nearby Vienna Airport.
Transport Minister Alexander Rezes has said an absence of a national airline costs Slovakia some two billion crowns a year.
Picha said SA will fly to many European destinations, but added that a significant focus will be placed on Russian customers, mainly in the field of tourism.
